title: Top 5 Most ICONIC Photos NASA Ever Took
hook: Number one is a single, lonely pixel captured from 6 billion kilometers away.

items.name: Blue Marble
items.stat: Shot by Apollo 17 in 1972 from about 29,000 km away, it's one of the most reproduced images in history.

items.name: The Hubble Deep Field
items.stat: A tiny dark patch of sky exposed for 10 days revealed roughly 3,000 galaxies.

items.name: Buzz Aldrin on the Moon
items.stat: Taken by Neil Armstrong in 1969, Armstrong himself is reflected in Aldrin's visor.

items.name: Pillars of Creation
items.stat: These towering columns of gas in the Eagle Nebula stand about 4 to 5 light-years tall.
items.query: Pillars of Creation Hubble Eagle Nebula

items.name: Pale Blue Dot
items.stat: Voyager 1 photographed Earth as a single pixel from 6 billion km away in 1990.
